concept.text: A proof that every simply connected, closed three-manifold is homeomorphic to the three-sphere. Proved by Grigori Perelman (2002–2003); the Clay Institute awarded the Millennium Prize in 2010, which he declined. Sources given: https://www.claymath.org/millennium-problems/ ; https://world-of-mathematics.com/blog/millennium-problems-overview/.

page.title: Proof of the Poincaré conjecture
page.definition: A proof that every closed, simply connected 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³, the unit sphere in four-dimensional Euclidean space. A 3-manifold is locally like ordinary 3-space; closed means compact without boundary, simply connected means connected with every loop contractible, and homeomorphic means related by a continuous bijection with continuous inverse.

goal.need: Recognizing S³ requires more than matching its homology groups, algebraic invariants of holes: Poincaré constructed a closed 3-manifold with the same homology but a fundamental group of order 120. The conjecture asks whether requiring every loop to contract suffices. CMI selected it among seven Millennium Prize Problems in 2000, each carrying US$1 million.

statements.quote: to emphasize the importance of working towards a solution of the deepest, most difficult problems
statements.context: The institute restated the purpose of its Millennium Prize Problems when announcing Perelman's award.

statements.quote: Thurston identified and analyzed 8 geometric structures and conjectured that they provide a means for classifying 3-manifolds.
statements.context: The IMU's Fields Medal account identifies the Poincaré conjecture as a special case of Thurston's geometrization conjecture.

completion.title: Clay awards its Millennium Prize for a proof that every closed, simply connected 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³.
completion.criterion: The Clay Mathematics Institute awards its Millennium Prize for a proof that every closed, simply connected topological 3-manifold is homeomorphic to S³. Clay’s rules allow an award only when the proof has been published in a qualifying outlet, at least 2 years have elapsed since publication and it has general acceptance in the mathematics community; advisory committees then recommend and the Board of Directors decides. Achieved: CMI announced its award to Grigori Perelman on 18 March 2010.
completion.set_by: Clay Mathematics Institute: the official problem description by John Milnor and the Millennium Prize rules, cited in their 2018 revision; the award is recorded in the announcement of 18 March 2010.
completion.threshold_quote: every simply connected closed 3-manifold is homeomorphic to the 3-sphere
completion.basis: CMI’s description fixes the proposition, and its rules make the award the institute’s own ruling that a published proof has general acceptance. The 2010 announcement states that the award followed the governing rules: recommendation by a Special Advisory Committee, then by the Scientific Advisory Board, with the final decision by the Board of Directors. It names the independent expositions and multi-year community scrutiny as the verification. The rules cited are the 2018 revision; the award was made under the rules in force in 2010. The 2006 Fields Medal and the expositions of 2006–2007 are evidence of acceptance, not the deciding event.

milestones.title: Every closed 3-manifold with positive Ricci curvature admits a metric of constant positive curvature.
milestones.criterion: Prove that every smooth closed 3-manifold admitting a Riemannian metric with strictly positive Ricci curvature also admits one with constant positive sectional curvature. For a simply connected manifold, this identifies the manifold with S³. Hamilton established the result in his peer-reviewed 1982 paper, Main Theorem 1.1.
milestones.set_by: Hamilton, Main Theorem 1.1 in Three-manifolds with positive Ricci curvature (1982); the field's convention of establishing a theorem by proof.
milestones.threshold_quote: Then X also admits a metric of constant positive curvature.

milestones.title: Ricci flow on a closed manifold cannot collapse locally at a finite singular time.
milestones.criterion: For any smooth Ricci flow g(t) on a closed n-manifold over 0 ≤ t < T < ∞, rule out sequences t_k → T and metric balls B_k = B(p_k,r_k) at time t_k for which r_k²/t_k stays bounded, |Rm| ≤ r_k⁻² throughout B_k, and Vol(B_k)/r_kⁿ → 0. Rm denotes the Riemann curvature tensor. Perelman stated this theorem in the preprint posted on 11 November 2002; Morgan–Tian provides a detailed treatment of noncollapse.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, no local collapsing theorem, §4.1 (2002), developed in Morgan and Tian's CMI/AMS exposition (2007); the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: If $M$ is closed and $T<\infty,$ then $g_{ij}(t)$ is not locally collapsing at $T.$

milestones.title: Every closed oriented 3-manifold admits Ricci flow with surgery for all t ≥ 0.
milestones.criterion: For every smooth closed oriented 3-manifold with any initial Riemannian metric, construct Ricci flow with surgery for all t ≥ 0, allowing extinction, with finitely many surgery times in each bounded time interval. Surgery cuts controlled necks and caps their boundaries; the allowed topological changes are specified in Morgan–Tian, Theorem 0.3. Perelman's construction was posted on 10 March 2003.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, §5.1 (2003); Morgan and Tian, Theorem 0.3 (2007), whose hypothesis includes all closed oriented 3-manifolds; the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: the Ricci flow with $\delta(t)$-cutoff is defined for $t\in[0,+\infty]$

milestones.title: Ricci flow with surgery becomes extinct in finite time on closed simply connected 3-manifolds.
milestones.criterion: For every initial Riemannian metric on a closed oriented 3-manifold whose prime decomposition contains no aspherical factors, the surgery flow becomes empty after some finite time T. Prime decomposition splits a manifold as a connected sum; an aspherical factor has contractible universal cover. This includes closed simply connected 3-manifolds. Perelman stated the theorem on 17 July 2003. Morgan–Tian's detailed exposition appeared in 2007; their correction was posted on 2 December 2015.
milestones.set_by: Perelman, Theorem 1.1 (2003); Morgan and Tian, Theorem 0.4 (2007), with their 2015 correction; the field's proof convention.
milestones.threshold_quote: the solution to the Ricci flow with surgery becomes extinct in finite time.

results.finding: For all smooth Ricci flows on closed n-manifolds, local collapse is ruled out at every finite time T.
results.detail: Theorem 4.1 uses exactly the specified bounds on radii and curvature and excludes normalized ball volumes tending to zero.

results.finding: For closed oriented 3-manifolds, Section 13.2 sketches continued Ricci flow with surgery and claims finitely many surgeries per finite time interval.
results.detail: The source outlines cutting off horns, capping, and restarting the flow, but defers the technically complicated surgery arguments. It does not supply the full construction and specified topological changes required by the criterion.
results.quote:
It turns out that those tips can be chosen in such a way that the need for the
surgery will arise only ﬁnite number of times on every ﬁnite t ime interval.

results.finding: For normalized closed oriented 3-manifolds, controlled surgery flows are κ-noncollapsed on all scales less than ε.
results.detail: Lemma 5.2 proves noncollapse under surgery cutoff and canonical neighborhood assumptions, using parabolic curvature bounds. It does not establish the stated arbitrary-dimensional theorem with spatial-ball curvature bounds; that earlier result is cited.
results.quote: Then it is κ-noncollapsed on all scales less than ǫ.

results.finding: Every smooth closed oriented 3-manifold admits surgery flow for all t ≥ 0, allowing extinction, with finitely many surgeries per bounded interval.
results.detail: Sections 4–5 construct controlled neck surgery and justify the assumptions globally. Normalization is obtainable by scaling any initial metric; cutoff parameters stay positive on finite intervals, and each surgery removes a definite volume.
results.quote:
Now since every surgery reduces t he volume by at
least h3, the sequence of surgery times is discrete, and, taking for gr anted the a
priori assumptions, we can continue our solution indeﬁnite ly, not ruling out the
possibility that it may become extinct at some ﬁnite time.

results.finding: Closed oriented 3-manifolds with initial λ > 0 admit surgery flows becoming extinct at T < ∞.
results.detail: Here λ is the first eigenvalue of −4△+R. The source proves extinction under this metric condition, including positive scalar curvature, but not for every initial metric on every manifold without aspherical prime factors.
results.quote:
If (M, gij) has λ > 0, then, for an appropriate choice of the cutoﬀ pa-
rameter, the solution becomes extinct in ﬁnite time.

results.finding: For compact 3-dimensional Ricci flows, the book establishes a positive noncollapse bound Vol(B(x,t,r)) ≥ κr³; sample size is not applicable.
results.detail: The supplied text uses a curvature bound throughout a backward parabolic neighborhood, stronger than the criterion's time-slice bound, and discusses dimension 3 rather than arbitrary n. It therefore establishes a restricted noncollapse result.
results.quote:
Hence,
these manifolds are non-collapsed at all points with a non-c ollapsing con-
stant that depends only on the geometry of the initial metric of the Ricci
ﬂow.

results.finding: Every closed oriented 3-manifold with any initial metric admits surgery flow for all t ≥ 0, with finitely many surgeries per bounded interval; sample size is not applicable.
results.detail: Theorem 0.3 applies whenever no locally separating RP² is embedded; the footnote explicitly includes every orientable manifold. It specifies the allowed topological changes, and the text proves surgery times cannot accumulate.
results.quote:
Then
there is a Ricci ﬂow with surgery deﬁned for all t ∈ [0, ∞) with initial metric
(M,g 0). The set of discontinuity times for this Ricci ﬂow with surge ry is
a discrete subset of [0, ∞).

results.finding: For every closed oriented 3-manifold without aspherical prime factors, surgery flow from any initial metric becomes empty at T < ∞; sample size is not applicable.
results.detail: Theorem 0.4 treats fundamental groups that are free products of finite and infinite cyclic groups. Corollary 0.5 and its proof identify this with the required prime-factor condition, including simply connected manifolds.
results.quote:
This Ricci ﬂow with surgery
becomes extinct after some time T <∞, in the sense that the manifolds Mt
are empty for all t ≥T .

results.finding: For every initial metric on any closed oriented 3-manifold with no aspherical prime factors, Ricci flow with surgery becomes extinct at a finite time T.
results.quote:
1.1 Theorem. Let M be a closed oriented three-manifold, whose prime decom-
position contains no aspherical factors. Then for any initi al metric on M the
solution to the Ricci ﬂow with surgery becomes extinct in ﬁni te time.

results.finding: CMI awarded Grigoriy Perelman the Millennium Prize for resolution of the Poincaré conjecture on 18 March 2010.
results.detail: The award followed recommendations by the Special Advisory Committee and Scientific Advisory Board, with the final decision by the Board of Directors.
results.quote:
The Clay Mathematics Institute hereby awards the Millennium Prize 
for resolution of the Poincaré conjecture to Grigoriy Perelman.
